items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Taking a walk after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. In one study, walking after dinner was linked to a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in sugar.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Having dinner before 8 pm is a good idea, as eating late is linked to a rise in sugar, with a difference of about 9.2 mg/dL. This was seen in the program and also in a check of real adults.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Averaging 14 hours of overnight fasting, like you did, is a good habit to keep, and it was part of a coaching program that changed some blood test results. In the program, adding an overnight fast to coaching changed one test result by -0.03 points compared to coaching alone.
